title: Log runtime/profile compatibility matrix at startup (hardware tuning profiles)
author: Quentin Harris
release_notes: - Runtime now logs a compact compatibility summary between the runtime build and the loaded hardware profile pack at startup. Helps detect misconfigured/unsupported profile packs in Private deployments before serving traffic.
description:
Problem: In Private deployments (and occasionally Dedicated), we’ve seen profile packs pinned/overridden without a clear signal that the selected profile version is outside the supported window for a given runtime build. The result is hard-to-triage behavior: silently ignored keys, default fallbacks, or degraded performance/latency. This PR adds an explicit compatibility matrix summary to runtime startup logs so operators can immediately confirm: (1) runtime build version, (2) profile pack version, (3) compatibility decision, and (4) the reason + recommended action. This is intentionally log-first (no API surface changes) and is safe for Hosted/Dedicated as well.

What changed (high level): Add a structured startup log line emitted after profile pack load + selection but before the server begins accepting traffic. The log includes: runtime_semver, runtime_git_sha, profile_pack_version, selected_profile_id, compatibility_status (compatible | compatible_with_warnings | incompatible | unknown), and a compact matrix of supported profile pack version ranges for this runtime. If the pack is incompatible, we still proceed with safe fallback semantics (existing behavior): we drop to baseline runtime defaults and emit an additional WARN with the fallback reason.

Log format: One structured JSON log event, key name `runtime.profile_compatibility`. We keep the matrix small and human-readable; it is not intended to be a full schema dump.

Example (single line): {"event":"runtime.profile_compatibility","runtime_version":"1.18.0","runtime_git_sha":"b7c1c63","profile_pack_version":"2025.12.0","selected_profile_id":"h100/balanced@2025.12.0","status":"compatible","supported_packs":["2025.11.x","2025.12.x"],"notes":["profile keys normalized","override_source=helm.values"]}

Why logs vs metrics: Metrics already exist for selected profile and override source (PR-22027). The compatibility decision is most useful at startup for operators doing upgrades/rollbacks; logs are easiest to capture during install/boot and in customer environments.

Tests: Unit tests cover: version range matching (exact/min/max), unknown runtime versions (dev builds), and matrix formatting stability. Integration test asserts: incompatible pack produces WARN + fallback status and does not crash startup.

Rollout: No config changes required. Private customers will see the new log line after upgrading to the runtime release containing this PR. SRE can use it during rollout to verify pack pinning and override order are doing what we expect.

Notes: No customer data is logged; this is strictly build/config metadata.

tests: add unit tests for compatibility matrix rendering and fallback behavior

conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee this runs after overrides are resolved? Otherwise the operator sees the wrong pack/version.
Quentin Harris (author): Yep. I moved emission to the end of `load_effective_profile_config()` after override precedence is applied. The log includes `override_source` (best-effort) for sanity.

Benji Okafor (review): Please keep the matrix bounded. I don’t want startup logs to grow unbounded across releases.
Quentin Harris: Agreed. The summary is capped to the last 3 supported pack minor lines for the current runtime (e.g., 2025.10/11/12). Also added a unit test to enforce the cap.

Diego Santos (review): How does this behave on dev builds where runtime version might be `0.0.0-dev`?
Quentin Harris: For dev builds we set status=unknown unless a runtime override `RUNTIME_SEMVER_OVERRIDE` is provided. This avoids false incompat warnings for local builds.

Neha Kapoor (SRE): If incompatible, do we fail closed? For Private, misconfig should be obvious.
Quentin Harris: We keep existing behavior (fail open to safe defaults) to avoid bricking deployments. We emit WARN with `status=incompatible` and `action=fall_back_to_runtime_defaults`. Runbook update recommends treating this as a release-blocker for customer rollouts.

Noah Patel (review): Please align naming with PR-22027 metrics (selected_profile_id, override_source).
Quentin Harris: Done. Keys now match the metric label names where possible.

Follow-up request (Ethan): Include a short remediation hint.
Quentin Harris: Added `recommended_action` field: `upgrade_runtime`, `downgrade_profile_pack`, or `remove_override`. Also included a linkable doc anchor in the troubleshooting page.

Approvals: Ethan Park (approved), Benji Okafor (approved), Diego Santos (approved), Neha Kapoor (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Backport not requested; will ship in next runtime release train.
